components.css: .ds-decision { overflow: hidden; width: 100%; border-radius: 16px; background: #f3f5f5; color: #17191b; font: 400 15px/1.45 "Schibsted Grotesk", "Helvetica Neue", Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; } .ds-decision__bar { min-height: 72px; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; gap: 1rem; padding: 1rem 1.25rem; background: #e5e9e9; } .ds-decision__bar p, .ds-decision__bar strong { display: block; margin: 0; } .ds-decision__body { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1.05fr 1fr .92fr; } .ds-decision__body section { min-width: 0; padding: clamp(1.35rem, 2.4vw, 2.25rem); } .ds-decision__body section + section { border-left: 1px solid #dfe0db; } .ds-decision h3 { margin: .3rem 0 1rem; color: #17191b; font-size: clamp(1.35rem, 2vw, 1.85rem); line-height: 1.1; letter-spacing: -.025em; } .ds-decision p { margin: 0; color: #454a4a; } .ds-label { display: block; color: #606565; font-size: 13px; font-weight: 600; } .ds-status { flex: none; padding: .3rem .58rem; border-radius: 999px; background: #fff2d7; color: #72470c; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 700; } .ds-decision:focus-within { outline: 3px solid #67d7ff; outline-offset: 4px; } @media (max-width: 640px) { .ds-decision { border-radius: 12px; } .ds-decision__body { grid-template-columns: 1fr; } .ds-decision__body section + section { border-left: 0; border-top: 1px solid #dfe0db; } }

narrative.overview:
Caimeo's design makes one consequential action legible from request to outcome. The visual system is direct, technical, and calm: near-black fields establish authority, light policy surfaces make the mechanism readable, and signal orange marks the one action that advances the conversation.

The page moves on one axis. Large claims lead into full-width proof, proof leads into an ordered sequence, and the sequence leads into a narrowly scoped call to action. Product evidence stays at useful scale; decoration never competes with the governed action.
keyCharacteristics: One linear reading path with no competing visual directions.
High-contrast dark and paper fields instead of decorative cards or glass.
Oversized, compact headlines paired with plainly written proof.
Square controls and data fields, with rounding reserved for the signature decision trace.
Restrained entrance and state motion that never obscures the evidence.

rules.name: The One-Trace Rule
rules.body: Lead with one concrete governed action and keep its request, policy, approvers, release state, and evidence visibly connected.

rules.name: The Rare Signal Rule
rules.body: Orange identifies the primary action or major transition; do not spread it across every heading, link, or product plate.

rules.name: The Semantic State Rule
rules.body: Green, red, and amber always retain their approval meanings and never become decorative brand colors.

rules.name: The One-Family Rule
rules.body: Create contrast through size, weight, and density; do not introduce a decorative display face or monospaced body copy.

rules.name: The Readable Proof Rule
rules.body: Operational evidence must remain body-sized and plainly labeled, even when adjacent marketing headlines are oversized.

rules.name: The Single-Axis Rule
rules.body: Every breakpoint preserves the same narrative order; responsive layout may stack or reorder paired media, but it must not create a second navigation or comparison mode.

rules.name: The Full-Size Proof Rule
rules.body: Product captures and the decision trace receive enough width to remain legible; do not shrink evidence into decorative thumbnails.

rules.name: The Flat Evidence Rule
rules.body: Keep proof on the page plane. Use field color and rules to separate states, not drop shadows, glass, glow, or blur.

rules.name: The Reserved Radius Rule
rules.body: Rounding belongs to the proof container and status labels; do not turn every section or product capture into a rounded card.

rules.name: The Honest State Rule
rules.body: A control may show an example outcome, but its copy must not imply that one click performed multiple real approvals.

dos: Do lead with one offer, one concrete trace, and one primary action.
Do keep approval state, policy reason, approvers, release boundary, and evidence readable in the same proof object.
Do preserve the dark-ground, light-field contrast and use signal orange sparingly.
Do keep supplied product captures large enough to read and pair each with concise explanatory copy.
Do preserve visible focus, semantic labels, keyboard operation, reduced-motion behavior, and mobile source order.
donts: Don't split the page into competing directions, feature-card grids, or chooser interactions before the offer is understood.
Don't use gradients, floating glass, decorative chrome, shadows, or metaphorical control-room ornament.
Don't scatter the approval sequence across unrelated panels or hide the release condition behind interaction.
Don't use semantic green, red, or amber as ambient decoration.
Don't add motion that delays reading, loops, or makes operational evidence shift while it is being inspected.
